context: Daichi and Tatsuya plan a fishing trip.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: たつや、釣り、本当、行こうか。
lines.en: Tatsuya, how about we really go fishing?
lines.style: Bright, open Kansai inflection on the proposal. Quick-paced warmth with a regional lilt. Genuine eagerness that invites without pressure—the sound of someone who already knows the answer will be yes.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Yeah. I've been really looking forward to it.
lines.style: Slow, measured response with the easy composure of someone unrushed. Low in register, steady. Warm but undemonstrative—the affirmation of someone who has already decided.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 一緒に、本当、頑張ろうな。
lines.en: Let's give it our all together, yeah?
lines.style: Kansai swing returning, warmer now—commitment underscoring the brightness. Quick-paced but lingering on the togetherness. Soft sincerity beneath the regional warmth.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.style: Quiet depth on 'grateful.' Rural slowness. Doesn't expand—lets the weight of years in that sentence settle. Tender without performance. Eye-level steadiness.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Emphatic double-pleasure on the repetition—the Kansai warmth peaking here. Light, genuine delight. No posturing. The sound of someone saying something true out loud.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.style: Mirror-calm to Daichi's peak. Quiet agreement that refuses to compete. Slow rural pace. Genuine, unadorned. The matching warmth of someone who doesn't need to say more.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Kansai inflection gentle on the closing. Promise held lightly, warmly. Slowing slightly—this is the moment. No pressure, just the sound of someone securing something precious.
